Anarchism is a political philosophy and movement that seeks to abolish all institutions that perpetuate authority, coercion, or hierarchy, primarily targeting the state and capitalism.

Battle of Moscow was a military campaign that consisted of two periods of strategically significant fighting on a 600 km (370 mi) sector of the Eastern Front during World War II, between October 1941 and January 1942.
This career academic taught international law in Cairo for three decades before serving as the UN's sixth secretary-general from 1992 to 1996, amid the Yugoslav breakup — who is he?
Boutros Boutros-Ghali (14 November 1922 - 16 February 2016) was an Egyptian politician and diplomat who served as the sixth secretary-general of the United Nations from 1992 to 1996.

A key figure in Japan's Meiji Restoration, this samurai later led a doomed 1877 uprising against the very government he helped create, dying in the fighting — who was he?
Saigō Takamori: Japanese samurai and politician (1828–1877)

Angered by how territory was divided after an earlier 1912-13 conflict, Bulgaria attacked its former allies Serbia and Greece in mid-1913, only to be beaten back on multiple fronts as Romania invaded from the north and the Ottomans reclaimed lost ground — which conflict?
Second Balkan War: Bulgaria's invasion of its neighbours (1913)
Dubbed the 'Father of Japanese capitalism,' this Meiji-era business magnate founded the country's first joint-stock bank and the Tokyo Stock Exchange — who is he?
The 33rd king and founder of the Tibetan Empire, he formally brought Buddhism to Tibet, built the Jokhang, and moved his capital to Lhasa while his minister devised the Tibetan script. Who was he?
Songtsen Gampo: 1st Tibetan Emperor and 33rd King of Tibet (d.650)

After her husband was arrested ahead of Belarus's 2020 election, this activist entered the presidential race in his place — a decision the regime allowed, wrongly assuming a woman couldn't mount a real challenge — who is she?
Sparked by the drowning of King Henry I's only legitimate son in the White Ship disaster, this 1138–1153 English succession war pitted Empress Matilda against Stephen of Blois — what is it called?
The Anarchy: Civil war in England and Normandy (1138–1153)
As first Grand Inquisitor of the Spanish Inquisition from 1478, this Dominican friar was also a chief supporter of the decree expelling Jews from Spain — who was he?
Tomás de Torquemada: Grand Inquisitor of Spain (1420–1498)

Going by VGE, this finance-minister-turned-president eked out a 1974 win over François Mitterrand with 50.8% of the vote, then liberalized French law on divorce, contraception, and abortion — who was he?
Valéry Giscard d'Estaing: President of France from 1974 to 1981.
Serving under Jimmy Carter, this Minnesota senator became the 42nd U.S. vice president and the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 1984 — who is he?
Walter Mondale: Vice President of the United States from 1977 to 1981.

Dubbed 'the Great Commoner' and 'the Boy Orator' for his faith in ordinary people and his thundering rhetoric, this Nebraskan was the Democrats' presidential nominee three times — in 1896, 1900, and 1908. Who was he?
This retired Turkish general served as the 30th Chief of the General Staff of the Turkish Armed Forces before becoming Minister of National Defense — who is he?
Yaşar Güler: Turkish general and politician (born 1954)
Son of Edward the Elder, this ruler is regarded by modern historians as the first King of England; he never married and was succeeded by his half-brother Edmund — who is he?
Æthelstan: King of the English from 927 to 939.
Which of these four is the eldest?

Oliver Heaviside (born 1850) is the earliest of the four. Although at odds with the scientific establishment for most of his life, Heaviside changed the face of telecommunications, mathematics, and science.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these four appeared first?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Pierre Curie is a physicist. Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 – 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
Which of these four is a chemist?
Mario Molina is a chemist. Mario José Molina-Pasquel Henríquez (19 March 1943 – 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Hydrogen?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
In what year was Hans Albert Einstein born?
Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
In what year was Mahmoud Ahmadinejad born?
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.
In what year was Kitty O'Neil born?
Kitty O'Neil: O'Neil subsequently moved into car racing and became a pioneering woman in the stunt industry in Hollywood.
In what year did Blaise Pascal die?
Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 – 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.
In what year did Milton Friedman die?
Milton Friedman: Friedman's challenges to what he called "naive Keynesian theory" began with his interpretation of consumption, which tracks how consumers spend.
In what year was Penicillin discovered?
Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by the Scottish physician Alexander Fleming as a crude extract of P. rubens.
In what year was Coulomb's law discovered?
Coulomb's law: This electric force is conventionally called the electrostatic force or Coulomb force.
Which company manufactures Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil?
Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil: Airbus Helicopters. The AS355 Ecureuil 2 is a twin-engine variant, marketed in North America as the TwinStar.
In which country is Junkers Ju 52?
Junkers Ju 52: Germany. Development of the Ju 52 commenced in the late 1920s, headed by German aeronautical engineer Ernst Zindel.
Who is credited with discovering Indium?
Indium: Ferdinand Reich. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Who is credited with discovering Californium?
Californium: Stanley Gerald Thompson. Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
Who is credited with discovering Fluorine?
Fluorine: Henri Moissan. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
This is the most common genetic cause of dwarfism, typically producing short arms and legs with a normal-length torso and an enlarged head with a prominent forehead — what condition is it?
Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder whose primary feature is dwarfism.
The twelfth-brightest star in our night sky and the brightest in the constellation Aquila. It's one of the three vertices of the Summer Triangle asterism. Name this star.

Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky. It has the Bayer designation Alpha Aquilae, which is Latinised from α Aquilae and abbreviated Alpha Aql or α Aql.
Whether contracted through the skin, the lungs, or the gut, this Bacillus-driven infection can take up to two months to show symptoms — what is it?
Anthrax is an infection caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis or Bacillus cereus biovar anthracis.
First described in 1740, this flowering-plant family rivals only the orchid family in sheer number of species, with over 32,000 recognized today — what family is it?
Asteraceae is a large family of flowering plants that consists of over 32,000 known species in over 1,900 genera within the order Asterales.
Designed to replace the aging Tu-126 'Moss,' this Soviet early-warning aircraft saw only about 42 built before the USSR's breakup ended production in 1992 — what is it?
Beriev A-50 (NATO reporting name: Mainstay) is a Soviet-origin airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft that is based on the Ilyushin Il-76 transport plane.
Every subatomic particle is either this integer-spin class or a fermion; Paul Dirac named the class after physicist Satyendra Nath Bose, whose statistics they obey — what's the class called?
Boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
Produced when quicklime is mixed with water, this white, powdery compound goes by many names in industry and food prep, where it's labeled E526 — what compound is it?
Calcium hydroxide (traditionally called slaked lime) is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Ca(OH)2.
Retired from Istanbul Technical University, this geologist holds foreign membership in both the US and Russian National Academies of Sciences. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör (born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.

This genus of flowering trees and shrubs, native to South and East Asia, Melanesia, and Australia, gave rise through extensive hybridization to oranges, lemons, grapefruits, and limes — what's the genus called?
Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the family Rutaceae.

What zoological term describes the internal-fertilization mating behavior in which a male animal introduces sperm directly into a female's reproductive tract — occurring via a 'cloacal kiss' in birds and most reptiles, or vaginally in mammals?
Copulation (zoology) is animal sexual behavior in which a male introduces sperm into the female's body, especially directly into the female's reproductive tract.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
This Penn professor's discoveries about modified nucleosides made the Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines possible, earning him a share of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine — who is he?
Drew Weissman (born September 7, 1959) is an American physician and immunologist known for his contributions to RNA biology.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Cats in this subfamily can purr but never roar, thanks to a bony rather than flexible hyoid bone — which subfamily?
Felinae are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.

Found from the tropics to subarctic regions and accounting for about 88% of living amphibian species, this tailless, semiaquatic creature has a name that informally splits into 'toad' for the warty ones — what is it?
Frog is any member of a diverse and largely semiaquatic group of short-bodied, tailless amphibian vertebrates composing the order Anura (coming from the Ancient Greek, literally 'without tail').
This ancient metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate through ten enzyme-catalyzed reactions in a cell's cytosol, generating ATP along the way. What process is it?
Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway that converts glucose (C6H12O6) into pyruvate and, in most organisms, occurs in the liquid part of cells (the cytosol).
Hailed by Time as a 2019 'Pioneer' yet condemned as a mad scientist, which Chinese biophysicist announced in 2018 that he'd created the first gene-edited human babies?
He Jiankui (pinyin: H Jinku HUH KWAY; born 1984) is a Chinese biophysicist known for his controversial first use of genome editing in humans in 2018.
One of the six Celtic nations, this peninsula in northwest France was known as Armorica under Roman rule before becoming an independent kingdom and later a duchy. What region is it?
Hydra (genus) is a genus of small freshwater hydrozoans in the phylum Cnidaria.
An ISO standard defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — and it's related to, but not the same as, invention. What word are we after?
Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.
A former Chicago financial options trader, this internet entrepreneur co-founded a nonprofit free encyclopedia as well as the for-profit wiki host Fandom — who is he?
Jimmy Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.
This American biologist and one-time Communist Party member had four husbands, the last being the physicist who led Los Alamos — who was she?
Kitty Oppenheimer (ne Puening; August 8, 1910 - October 27, 1972) was an American biologist, botanist, and a member of the Communist Party of America until leaving in the 1930s.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 claiming a birth year of 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists now regard as myth — who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen (simplified; traditional; pinyin: L Qngyn, died 6 May 1933) was a Chinese herbalist, martial artist and tactical advisor, known for his supposed extreme longevity.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
Among the first women in Canada to earn a medical doctorate, this physician-chemist is best remembered for a landmark 1913 enzyme-kinetics paper co-authored with Leonor Michaelis — who was she?
Maud Menten (March 20, 1879 - July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.

This large-scale industrial activity extracts everything from coal and gemstones to rock salt and potash from the Earth, providing raw materials that can't be grown or feasibly manufactured — what is this activity called?
Mining is the extraction of geological materials and minerals from Earth's surface.
Named from the Ancient Greek for 'mouse's ear' after its foliage's shape, this genus of small blue Northern Hemisphere flowers serves as Alaska's official state flower — what's the genus?
Myosotis is a genus of flowering plants in the borage family Boraginaceae.
Containing turbinates and olfactory mucosa within its cavity, this organ centers the human face and provides an alternate airway while infants nurse — which body part?
Nose is a sensory organ and respiratory structure in vertebrates.
This bivalve mollusk is prized both as a delicacy on the half shell and, in certain species, for the pearls it produces inside its shell — what is it?
Oyster is the common name for a number of different families of salt-water bivalve molluscs that live in marine or brackish habitats.
Named from Greek words for 'odd' and 'toe,' this mammalian order groups horses, rhinoceroses, and tapirs together based on their toe count. Which order?
Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek, perisss 'odd' and, dktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
A member of the cashew family and a priority tree-nut allergen, this green seed saw the US, Iran, and Turkey produce 87% of the world's 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — what is it?
Pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.
Split into the strepsirrhines — lemurs and lorisids — and the haplorhines — tarsiers, monkeys and apes — this order ranges in size down to tiny Madame Berthe's — what is it?

Primate is an order of mammals, which is further divided into the strepsirrhines, which include lemurs, galagos, and lorisids; and the haplorhines, which include tarsiers and simians (monkeys and apes).

Founding an organization promoting swadeshi economics against globalization, this Indian social activist later allied with a yoga guru to combine that economic message with the promotion of yoga and Ayurveda — who is he?
Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 - 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.
Named for its type genus, this plant family of nearly 4,800 species includes the trees and shrubs behind apples, pears, plums, cherries, and peaches — what family is it?
Rosaceae is a family of flowering plants that includes 4,828 known species in 91 genera.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

Known for a leather-like smell when freshly milled and prized for durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood tree bears small, fragrant white flowers and large, papery, often-hairy leaves — name this tree?
Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood tree species in the family Lamiaceae.

A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid that helps give gasoline and paint fumes their aroma, this benzene relative — a methyl group on a phenyl ring — serves as paint thinner and industrial solvent. What is it?
Toluene is a substituted aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C6H5CH3, often abbreviated as PhCH3, where Ph stands for the phenyl group.

This membrane-bound organelle, found in plant and fungal cells and some others, is essentially a water-filled storage compartment with no fixed shape, formed when smaller membrane vesicles fuse together. What is it called?
Vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle which is present in plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.

This American physical chemist built ultra-sensitive Geiger counters and once worked on the Manhattan Project — but his 1960 Nobel came for a dating method that revolutionized archaeology and paleontology. Who was he?

Willard Libby (December 17, 1908 - September 8, 1980) was an American physical chemist noted for his role in the 1949 development of radiocarbon dating, a process which revolutionized archaeology and palaeontology.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
Prized for its oil since Spanish and Portuguese traders carried it from South America to Europe in the 1600s, this citrus-scented herb also goes by 'beebrush' — what's its species name?
Aloysia citrodora: Species of plant. Aloysia citrodora, lemon verbena, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
A towering 20th-century French mathematician known for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, he was a principal founder of the Bourbaki group. Who was he?

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, this group flies on long digits webbed with a thin membrane and makes up about 20% of all classified mammals — what are they?

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
Holding the title of smallest great ape, this creature has pinker lips and a darker face than its close cousin, and was once dismissed as merely a 'pygmy' subspecies of it — what is it?
Bonobo: Species of great ape. Taxonomically, members of the chimpanzee/bonobo subtribe Panina—composed entirely by the genus Pan—are collectively termed panins.
Nicknamed 'the lawyer' and 'freshwater cod,' this coldwater fish is the only member of its genus and the sole freshwater species in its entire order — what fish is it?
Burbot: Species of fish. The species is closely related to marine fish such as the common ling and cusk, all of which belong to the family Lotidae (rocklings).
Also known as Flinders rose, this perennial shrub with rounded fleshy leaves and white-to-pink flowers is native across circum-Mediterranean countries — what's the plant called?
Marketed as a COX-2 inhibitor, this NSAID treats arthritis pain and menstrual cramps but carries heart attack and stroke risk warnings — which drug?

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
This medium-to-large sea snail's shell tapers to a noticeable point at both ends thanks to its high spire and siphonal canal — what type of shelled creature is it?
Conch: Shell or sea snails. Conch (US: KONK, KONCH, UK: KONCH) is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the trachea and announces itself with an unmistakable barking, brassy cough — what's it called?
Croup: Respiratory infection often caused by a virus.

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This number-theory rule holds that if p is prime, then for any integer a, the value a to the power p minus a is always a multiple of p — which rule is this?

Fermat's little theorem: A prime p divides a^p–a for any integer a. Fermat's little theorem is the basis for the Fermat primality test and is one of the fundamental results of elementary number theory.
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, these lizards are unusual for making vocal chirps and clicks, and most lack eyelids, relying on a transparent membrane instead — what are they?
Gecko: Lizards belonging to the suborder Gekkota.
Brought to market by Monsanto in 1974 under the brand name Roundup, this herbicide works by blocking a key enzyme that plants need to grow — what is it?
Glyphosate: Systemic herbicide and crop desiccant.
A founder of psychophysics, this German scientist captured how sensation relates to stimulus in a logarithmic law that now bears his and Weber's names — who was he?
Gustav Fechner: German experimental psychologist, physicist, and philosopher (1801–1887)

Spun into usable fiber some 50,000 years ago and, alongside bamboo, among the fastest-growing plants on Earth, which Cannabis sativa crop is grown for rope, paper, textiles and biofuel rather than for getting high?
These giant wasps of the genus Vespa build communal nests from chewed wood pulp, with one Asian species growing past two inches long — what are they called?

When the thyroid produces too little hormone, the body slows down — cold intolerance, fatigue, constipation, weight gain — and worldwide too little dietary iodine is the leading cause. What's the condition?
Hypothyroidism: Insufficient production of thyroid hormones.
Known naturally as the mineral hematite, this reddish compound with formula Fe2O3 is the main source for the steel industry and gets reduced by aluminum in the fiery thermite reaction — what is it?
Iron(III) oxide: Chemical compound. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
This businessman and chemist owned the Lakers through their 1980s 'Showtime' era, winning 10 NBA titles before a Hall of Fame induction as a contributor — who was he?
Jerry Buss: American businessman and investor (1933–2013)
The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, she served as a mission specialist on two Space Shuttle Columbia flights, the second ending in the 2003 disaster that killed her — who was she?
This plant family — home to basil, rosemary, thyme, lavender, and sage — also counts teak among its rare tree species and chia among its edible seed crops — which family?
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
This sexually dimorphic East Asian perching waterfowl, closely related to North America's wood-dwelling cousin, gets its species name from a Latin word for a wig — which bird?
Mandarin duck: Species of bird. The mandarin duck (Aix galericulata) is a perching duck species native to East and Northeast Asia.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
Named from Greek words for 'small' and 'head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-average head size and can result from genetic syndromes or prenatal toxin exposure — what is it?
Microcephaly: Condition in which the head is small due to an underdeveloped brain.

Étienne Geoffroy split these simians into 'Old World' Catarrhini and 'New World' Platyrrhini groups, and counting them without the apes leaves a famously incomplete family tree — what common-name animal is this?
Monkey: Animal of the "higher primates", excluding apes.
Native to southern Europe and North Africa, this fragrant evergreen shrub has berries that are macerated in alcohol to make Mirto liqueur — which plant?
Myrtus communis: Species of flowering plant.
Present in 26 African countries with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana, which large crocodilian sees adult males reach 3.5 to 5 metres long?
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.

First described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the "cellar spider" and "vibrating spider" — and shares a famous leggy nickname with harvestmen and crane flies. What family is it?
Pholcidae: Family of spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
Sometimes called a 'collapsed lung,' this condition involves air trapped in the space between the lung and chest wall, causing sudden sharp one-sided chest pain — what is it?
Pneumothorax: Abnormal collection of air in the pleural space.
Manufactured in a soybean-oil emulsion that gives it a milky white look, this IV anesthetic — sold as Diprivan — induces unconsciousness fast and lets patients wake quickly; what is it?
Propofol: Intravenous medication used in anesthesia.
Guided by empiricist and positivist philosophy, which academic methodology turns data collection into numbers to test theories across the natural, applied, formal, and social sciences?
Quantitative research: All procedures for the numerical representation of empirical facts.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this non-venomous constrictor is the world's longest snake and has been spotted swimming far out at sea — what species is it?
Reticulated python: Species of snake. It is the world's longest snake, and the third heaviest after the green anaconda and Burmese python.

Sold under the brand name Crestor, this medication lowers cholesterol by inhibiting an enzyme in the liver called HMG-CoA reductase, and was the twelfth most commonly prescribed drug in the US in 2023. What is it?
Rosuvastatin: Statin medication. It is recommended to be used with dietary changes, exercise, and weight loss.
Also called a green onion, this mild Allium vegetable has a slender green stem but never develops a bulb like its garlic and leek relatives — what is it?
Scallion: Edible vegetable of various species in the genus Allium.
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)
Known as caustic soda or lye, this white ionic solid is so corrosive it breaks down fats and proteins at room temperature and eagerly drinks moisture from the air — what compound is it?
Sodium hydroxide: Caustic soda, with formula NaOH.
This physics law states that a black body's radiated energy per unit area is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature — which law?
Stefan–Boltzmann law: Physical law on the emissive power of black body.
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
The primary male sex hormone, this androgen builds muscle and bone, spurs body hair, and is even linked to mood, courtship display and dominance in both sexes — what is it?
Testosterone: Primary male sex hormone. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
Named after the Turkish word for turban, which it was thought to resemble, this spring-blooming bulb belongs to the lily family and includes about 75 species — which flower?
The primary flavor compound in the vanilla bean, this phenolic aldehyde is now more often made synthetically than extracted from the real pod — what is it?
Vanillin: Chemical compound. Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
Named after the German city where it originated, this all-purpose gun dog breed was officially recognized in 1891 — what breed is it?
Weimaraner: German breed of dog. The Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
